title: Working with Anita O'Day
summary: Anita O'Day asks for him after Michael's Pub, he tours Europe and Japan and records at Vine Street, and they become drinking partners.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Let me give you some, let’s move on into Anita O’Day.
Now this is a — I did a record with her out in California.

For some reason she came in to the picture because it’s a Gene Krupa legend. They were trying to — I call it “humping the grave.” They just keep trying to hump the grave you know. So now like here is Anita O’Day playing at Michael’s Pub in New York. And I had worked with her with the Buddy Rich band at the Blue Note. And they brought some drummer in from Boston, who, I don’t know whatever happened, I don’t even know who he was or what he was, but he lasted about one night and she was pretty rough to deal with. And so she remembered me and she said, “get that drummer that was with Buddy Rich’s band.” So I went in and worked with her at Michael’s Pub for ten weeks, something like that. And then I went on the road with her. Went to Europe with her and went to Japan a couple of times with her, and recorded with her out at Vine Street with Pete Jolly and all those guys. But man, did she and I ever become drinking partners. Wooh. And she could drink. But one time man, see I used to have this thing what I call the “wet season” and a “dry season.” From January 1st to July 4th, I would not even eat
rum cake. But then July 4th until January 2nd I would drink at least a quart of vodka a day. And that went on for years and years and years.
